inspiration: A particle emitter as a data record: start time, stop time, emit rate, speed with random spread, and lifetime in one controller (include/niflib/ni_particles.h:88-113). A blood spurt or spark burst as one small record.
Typed records looked up by name: a block factory builds 100 record types from their type names (README.md, Port Status). Use for effect and unit records looked up by name.
Fail loud on unknown data: unknown block types fail with an explicit error (README.md, Port Status). Our loaders can do the same for unknown effect or zone keys.
Skinning and morph targets are separate record files (ni_skinning.h, ni_morph.h). Morph targets could blend a creature pose without a full rig. File names only.
Collision and extra-data records are separate from geometry (ni_collision.h, ni_extra_data.h). Hit shapes as data on the model. File names only.

briefs.label: Spark burst from a controller record
briefs.why: A short, dense burst reads as an impact. A data record lets us tune it without code.
briefs.keep: Start and stop window; emit rate; speed spread; lifetime
briefs.change: Our own shape and colour; no file-format tie; our own timing curve

briefs.label: Pose blend by morph targets
briefs.why: Blending a few sculpted poses gives a creature weight without a full skeleton.
briefs.keep: Named target shapes; a weight per target
briefs.change: Our own target set; fewer targets; our own blend rules

briefs.label: Hit shapes stored on the model
briefs.why: Hit shapes kept as data on the model keep combat tuning out of code.
briefs.keep: Collision record separate from geometry; per-model data
briefs.change: Our own shape types; our own hit-zone names
